title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This is not a model error or a deployment failure. It is a person using generative image tools to fabricate sexually explicit pictures of a real woman, whose photographs he took from her private social media account. The fabrication was paired with impersonation: the material was circulated through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord and Facebook, and multiple Gmail addresses were used to keep the operator's identity hidden. The harm came from the combination, a synthetic image of an identifiable person plus a distribution channel that concealed who was behind it.

The point of failure sits at the level of an individual user, not inside a product pipeline. Nothing in the reporting describes a check by any platform or model that flagged the images before they circulated. Detection came afterwards and from outside: the woman reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after anonymous accounts told her the material was on Discord servers, and police reconstructed the trail from social media accounts and email records. Catching this earlier would have required either a platform-side check on the fabricated images or on the account and email patterns, and the reporting does not say whether any such check existed.

What is not established is guilt. An arrest is not a conviction, and the account Bansal gave in interrogation, that personal resentment drove him, is his own statement rather than a finding. The other users he said created additional explicit content and he reshared are not identified in the reporting.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing sexually explicit artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate, obtained photos from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create obscene morphed images. He then shared this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The case began when the 22-year-old victim reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her manipulated photos and videos were being circulated on Discord servers. Police conducted a digital investigation, analyzing social media accounts and email trails to identify Bansal. During interrogation, he admitted he knew the woman from college and claimed personal resentment motivated his actions. He also disclosed that other online users created additional explicit content that he subsequently reshared. Police recovered his mobile phone and other digital evidence related to the case.
